findings.who: A filer born after 1936 who, as an alternate payee under a QDRO, received their former spouse's whole plan balance in 2025. The former spouse is the plan participant and was born in 1933.
findings.why_no: The parenthetical '(you, or the person you inherited it from)' reads as the complete list. The filer did not inherit the balance and was born after 1936, so they answer about themselves and say no.
findings.irs_text: i1040gi p. 30, Lump-Sum Distributions TIP: 'If you or the plan participant was born before January 2, 1936, you could pay less tax on the distribution. See Form 4972.'
findings.fix: Ask about the plan participant, the employee whose plan it was, and say this covers you, your spouse, a former spouse whose plan was divided by a court order (QDRO), or anyone who died and left it to you, directly or through another heir.

findings.who: A successor beneficiary. The filer inherited the plan balance from their mother (born 1942), who had inherited it from her husband, the participant (born 1931). The whole balance was paid out in 2025.
findings.why_no: 'The person you inherited it from' points to the mother, who was born after 1936, so the filer answers no. The participant whose birth date controls is never asked about.
findings.irs_text: i1040gi p. 30: 'If you or the plan participant was born before January 2, 1936, you could pay less tax on the distribution. See Form 4972.'
findings.fix: Ask whether the original plan participant (the employee who earned the benefit, even if it passed through more than one heir) was born before January 2, 1936.

findings.who: On a joint return, the spouse (born 1934) received a total distribution of their own plan balance. The primary filer (born 1950) answers the interview for that spouse's Form 1099-R.
findings.why_no: The words 'you, or the person you inherited it from' lead the filer to answer about their own birth date (1950) and say no, although the spouse earned the plan.
findings.irs_text: i1040gi p. 30: 'If you or the plan participant was born before January 2, 1936, you could pay less tax on the distribution. See Form 4972.'
findings.fix: Name the recipient of each Form 1099-R and ask about that person's plan participant, for example: 'Was the employee who earned this plan balance (you, your spouse, or the person it came from) born before January 2, 1936?'

locators: pp. 27-30, lines 4a-5b: Exceptions 2-4, Lump-Sum Distributions, Insurance Premiums for Retired Public Safety Officers, Simplified Method

findings.who: The beneficiary of an employee who died before August 21, 1996, now receiving a survivor annuity from a plan the employee funded only with pre-tax or employer money. The beneficiary is entitled to the death benefit exclusion of up to $5,000.
findings.why_no: No money paid into the plan was ever taxed when it went in, and there are no after-tax contributions. The truthful answer to the question as worded is No, even though the instructions treat the death benefit exclusion as part of the cost.
findings.irs_text: i1040gi p. 29, Simplified Method Worksheet, Before you begin: "If you are the beneficiary of a deceased employee or former employee who died before August 21, 1996, include any death benefit exclusion that you are entitled to (up to $5,000) in the amount entered on line 2 below."
findings.fix: Ask a broader cost gate: "Do you have any cost (tax-free basis) in this pension or annuity? This includes after-tax contributions by you or the person who earned the pension, an amount in box 5 or box 9b, or, if you are the beneficiary of an employee who died before August 21, 1996, a death benefit exclusion." Add a separate yes/no about a death before August 21, 1996 for beneficiaries.

findings.who: A widow or other beneficiary receiving a survivor annuity under a joint and survivor pension. The retiree, now deceased, made after-tax contributions. The survivor's Form 1099-R may leave box 5 and box 9b blank.
findings.why_no: The survivor never paid anything into the plan and reads "money paid into this pension" and "after-tax contributions" as their own. With the boxes blank, they answer No.
findings.irs_text: p575 p. 34, Survivors of retirees: "If the retiree was reporting the annuity under the Simplified Method, the part of each payment that is tax free is the same as the tax-free amount figured by the retiree at the annuity starting date"; i1040gi p. 30: "If you are the survivor of a retiree, use the retiree's age"
findings.fix: Say "by you or by the person who earned this pension (for a survivor or beneficiary, the deceased employee or retiree)". Tell survivors to check the retiree's prior-year returns or worksheets.

findings.who: A retiree whose payer leaves box 5 and box 9b blank and checks box 2b "taxable amount not determined". This is common for older or governmental plans, and in later years after the first. The retiree has records of after-tax contributions.
findings.why_no: The help says "An amount in box 5 or box 9b means yes." A filer reads the boxes as the test, sees them blank, and answers No.
findings.irs_text: i1040gi p. 28: "If your Form 1099-R doesn't show the taxable amount, you must use the General Rule ... But if your annuity starting date ... was after July 1, 1986, see Simplified Method"; p. 30, Cost: "Your net investment may be shown in box 9b"
findings.fix: Add: "Blank boxes do not mean No. Answer Yes if your records, a prior year's Simplified Method Worksheet, or the plan show after-tax contributions, or if box 2b 'taxable amount not determined' is checked and you are unsure."

findings.who: An employee whose cost includes employer amounts that were taxed to them when made. Examples are the cost of life insurance protection under the plan included in their wages, or employer contributions reported as income. The employee made no voluntary after-tax contributions.
findings.why_no: The parenthetical "(after-tax contributions)" reads as the employee's own after-tax deposits, so the filer answers No.
findings.irs_text: i1040gi p. 30, Cost: "Your cost is generally your net investment in the plan ... It doesn't include pre-tax contributions"; p. 30, Rollovers: "subtract any contributions (usually shown in box 5) that were taxable to you when made"
findings.fix: Reword: "Was any amount put into this plan taxed to you when it went in? This includes your after-tax contributions and any employer amounts reported as income to you at the time."

findings.who: A person receiving payments from a commercial annuity they bought themselves from an insurance company with savings (a nonqualified annuity).
findings.why_no: The filer does not think of buying a policy with savings as money "already taxed when it went in" or as "contributions". Box 5 and box 9b may be blank or confusing, so they answer No. The tool then misses the refusal at retirement.own_annuity and fully taxes the payments.
findings.irs_text: i1040gi p. 28: "Your payments are fully taxable if (a) you didn't contribute to the cost (see Cost, later) of your pension or annuity"; p. 30, Simplified Method condition 2a limits it to qualified employee plans, qualified employee annuities and tax-sheltered annuities
findings.fix: Ask retirement.own_annuity before the cost gate, not under it. Or add to the gate: "If you bought this annuity yourself with your own savings, answer Yes."

findings.who: A retiree receiving periodic payments from a designated Roth account in a 401(k) or 403(b) that are not a qualified distribution.
findings.why_no: The filer thinks of Roth money as untaxed and does not see Roth deferrals as "already taxed" contributions, so they answer No.
findings.irs_text: i1040gi p. 30, Cost: "Your cost is generally your net investment in the plan ... It doesn't include pre-tax contributions"; p. 30: subtract "any contributions (usually shown in box 5) that were taxable to you when made"
findings.fix: Add: "Roth 401(k) or Roth 403(b) contributions count as already taxed."

locators: p. 30, Simplified Method, conditions 1 and 2; p. 28, Partially Taxable Pensions and Annuities; , Distribution On or After Annuity Starting Date, "If you receive a nonperiodic payment from your annuity contract on or after the annuity starting date, you must generally include all of the payment in gross income."; , Survivors of retirees, "If the retiree was reporting the annuity under the Simplified Method, the part of each payment that is tax free is the same as the tax-free amount figured by the retiree at the annuity starting date"
pp. 27-30, lines 4a-5b: Exceptions 2-4, Lump-Sum Distributions, Insurance Premiums for Retired Public Safety Officers, Simplified Method

used.how: pages named by another document's citation

findings.who: A joint filer, age 66, whose spouse, age 48, received a disability pension in 2025 on a Form 1099-R issued to the spouse. The spouse's employer plan sets its minimum retirement age at 55.
findings.why_no: The gate asks 'were you younger than the earliest age at which the plan would have let you retire'. The person answering reads 'you' as themselves, the primary filer, who is past any retirement age, and truthfully answers no. The parent question ('paid to you because you became disabled') has the same wording, so the error starts there too.
findings.irs_text: i1040gi p. 28: 'Don't include the following payments on lines 5a and 5b. Instead, report them on line 1h. • Disability pensions received before you reach the minimum retirement age set by your employer.'
findings.fix: Name the recipient of this Form 1099-R: 'When any of this was paid, was the person this Form 1099-R was issued to (you or your spouse) younger than ...'. Use the same wording in the parent disability question.

findings.who: A filer whose plan's minimum retirement age is 60. They turned 60 in June 2025, so the January to May payments came before that age and the later ones came after it.
findings.why_no: The filer is now past the age, and the form that reports 'this' arrived in 2026. They read 'were you younger' as asking about their status now, or about the year as a whole, and answer no. The gated question is then never asked, so the No that should end the interview (a year in which the filer reached that age is outside what the tool prepares) never happens. The pre-age payments are reported as a pension instead of as wages.
findings.irs_text: i1040gi p. 25: 'Disability pensions shown on Form 1099-R if you haven't reached the minimum retirement age set by your employer ... Disability pensions received after you reach minimum retirement age ... are reported on lines 5a and 5b'
findings.fix: Ask: 'Was even one 2025 payment on this form made before the day you reached the plan's minimum retirement age? Answer yes if you reached that age during 2025.'

findings.who: A 57-year-old receiving a disability pension from a plan that allows no retirement before 60. The filer does not know the plan's age.
findings.why_no: The filer substitutes a familiar age instead: 55, or the 59½ age for penalty-free distributions. Believing they are past it, they answer no. No help text tells them where to find the plan's age or that it differs from these ages.
findings.irs_text: i1040gi p. 28: 'Disability pensions received before you reach the minimum retirement age set by your employer.'
findings.fix: Add help text: 'This is the age set by your employer's plan, found in the plan documents or obtainable from the plan administrator. It is not 59½, Social Security's retirement age, or the plan's normal retirement age.' Alternatively, ask for the plan's minimum retirement age and the filer's birth date, and compute the answer.

findings.who: A disabled filer, age 58, in a plan whose early retirement age is 55 and whose normal retirement age is 62.
findings.why_no: This is a borderline reading rather than a wrong no. Some filers read 'earliest age ... without the disability' as the plan's normal retirement age. That reading produces a wrong yes, not a wrong no. The opposite case is a plan that allows early retirement only after a service requirement the filer had not met. That filer may still answer no, keying on age alone.
findings.irs_text: i1040gi p. 25: 'minimum retirement age set by your employer'
findings.fix: Define the age as 'the earliest age at which you personally could have started receiving a pension from this plan, given your service, had you not become disabled'.

locators: p. 25, "Disability pensions received after you reach minimum retirement age and other payments shown on Form 1099-R (other than payments from an IRA) are reported on lines 5a and 5b"

p. 25, "Disability pensions shown on Form 1099-R if you haven’t reached the minimum retirement age set by your employer", "Disability pensions received after you reach minimum retirement age and other payments shown on Form 1099-R (other than payments from an IRA) are reported on lines 5a and 5b"
pp. 27-30, lines 4a-5b: Exceptions 2-4, Lump-Sum Distributions, Insurance Premiums for Retired Public Safety Officers, Simplified Method

findings.who: A joint filer whose spouse retired early on disability from an employer pension plan and is below the plan's minimum retirement age. The spouse's Form 1099-R is entered in the retirement document, but the filer is the one answering.
findings.why_no: The gate asks whether this was paid 'to you because you became disabled.' The filer is not disabled and was paid nothing, so a truthful no follows. The spouse's disability pension then stays on lines 5a/5b instead of moving to line 1h.
findings.irs_text: i1040gi 2025 p. 28, Lines 5a and 5b: "Don't include the following payments on lines 5a and 5b. Instead, report them on line 1h. • Disability pensions received before you reach the minimum retirement age set by your employer."
findings.fix: Name the recipient of the document: "Was any of this paid to [you / your spouse] because [you / they] became disabled, under a plan that provides for disability retirement?" Alternatively, say in the help that on a joint return the question is about the person shown on the Form 1099-R.

findings.who: A joint filer whose spouse receives a military disability retirement pension from DFAS, or whose spouse was disabled in a terrorist attack and receives a disability pension.
findings.why_no: "Because you became disabled" reads as being about the filer, so a truthful no follows. The military and terrorist-attack questions are never asked, and the refusal they lead to is missed.
findings.irs_text: i1040gi 2025 p. 28: "For details on military disability pensions, see Pub. 525." p. 30: "You must include in your income any amounts that you received that you would have received in retirement had you not become disabled as a result of a terrorist attack."
findings.fix: Same as above: name the spouse explicitly, or ask about the person shown on the Form 1099-R.

findings.who: A military retiree, or the spouse of one, who was retired for disability (for example, a medical retirement under 10 U.S.C. chapter 61). The retired pay comes from DFAS on a Form 1099-R.
findings.why_no: They do not think of military retired pay as being paid 'under a plan that provides for disability retirement.' Military pay is not a 'plan' with a plan document or an employer. They answer no, and the out-of-scope refusal for an armed-forces disability pension is never reached.
findings.irs_text: i1040gi 2025 p. 28: "Fully taxable pensions and annuities also include military retirement pay shown on Form 1099-R. For details on military disability pensions, see Pub. 525."
findings.fix: Before the gate, ask every pension recipient: "Is this retired pay from the armed forces (for example, a Form 1099-R from DFAS or the Coast Guard)?" Then ask whether any of it is based on disability. Alternatively, add to the gate's help: "Military retired pay for disability counts."

findings.who: A filer who stopped working because of a disability and began receiving payments from an employer pension. They do not know whether the plan formally 'provides for disability retirement.' Their Form 1099-R shows distribution code 3 in box 7.
findings.why_no: Whether a plan 'provides for disability retirement' is a legal feature of the plan document that the filer cannot check. Unsure, they answer no, and a disability pension received before the minimum retirement age is not moved to line 1h.
findings.irs_text: i1040gi 2025 p. 30: "If you receive payments from a retirement or profit-sharing plan that does not provide for disability retirement, do not treat those payments as disability payments." p. 28: "Disability pensions received before you reach the minimum retirement age set by your employer" go on line 1h.
findings.fix: First ask what the filer can check: "Does box 7 of the Form 1099-R show code 3, or did the plan begin paying you because you became disabled?" On a yes, ask whether the plan provides for disability retirement, with help saying the plan administrator can confirm this.

findings.who: A filer disabled in a terrorist attack (for example, the 9/11 cleanup contractor in the IRS example). Their plan pays the normal retirement benefit early on account of disability. They view the payment as an ordinary early-retirement pension that they elected.
findings.why_no: They read 'paid to you because you became disabled' as excluding a pension they chose to start at the plan's early retirement age. They answer no, and the terrorist-attack question and its refusal are skipped.
findings.irs_text: i1040gi 2025 p. 30, Example: "The pension plan provides that a participant who retires early on account of disability is entitled to receive the participant's normal retirement benefit... you can exclude $500 of your monthly retirement benefit from income."
findings.fix: Add help to the gate: "Answer yes if the plan started payments, or pays a larger amount, because of your disability, even if you were also old enough for early retirement."

locators: pp. 27-30, lines 4a-5b: Exceptions 2-4, Lump-Sum Distributions, Insurance Premiums for Retired Public Safety Officers, Simplified Method

findings.who: A filer whose Form 1099-R box 7 shows code 2 together with a second code, such as 2B, 2D, 2K, 2L (a loan offset), 2M, 2P or 28. Some of the money is not covered by the exception.
findings.why_no: The gate tests whether the box 7 code helper equals the single value 'early_exception_2'. If the helper stores a two-character entry as another value, or keeps only the other code, the computed condition is false. The partial-coverage question is then never asked and the line is set to false.
findings.irs_text: i5329 (2025) p. 5, Line 2: "Enter on line 2 the amount that you can exclude." Only the excludable part of an early distribution escapes the additional tax.
findings.fix: Compute the gate as 'any code entered in box 7 is 2', so combinations like 2B, 2D, 2K, 2L, 2M, 2P and 28 also trigger it. Or ask the partial-coverage question for any box 7 entry that contains 2.

findings.who: A filer under 59 1/2 taking substantially equal periodic payments that the payer codes 2. During 2025 they changed the payment amount or took an extra withdrawal before the series ended.
findings.why_no: The help says code 2 means the payer knows of an exception. The filer believes this year's payment is part of the series and answers no. They don't realize the modification ends the exception for this year, and that the recapture of earlier years' tax is also outside the tool's scope.
findings.irs_text: i5329 (2025) p. 5, exception 02: "Distributions made as part of a series of substantially equal periodic payments (made at least annually) for your life (or life expectancy)..."
findings.fix: Add to the help: 'Answer Yes if you changed or stopped a series of substantially equal payments this year, or took more than the scheduled amount.' Or ask directly whether a periodic-payment series was modified.

findings.who: A filer with a code 2 distribution for a dollar-capped exception who already used part of the cap in an earlier year. For example, a birth or adoption distribution for a child who got a 2024 distribution too, or a first-home IRA withdrawal after an earlier one. A spouse's distribution for the same child is counted separately.
findings.why_no: The filer sees code 2 and an amount within the cap for this year's form alone. They read 'this money' as this year's form and do not add the earlier year's distribution.
findings.irs_text: i5329 (2025) p. 5, exception 19: "a distribution of up to $5,000 if made during the 1-year period beginning on the date your child was born or adopted". Exception 09: "IRA distributions made for the purchase of a first home, up to $10,000."
findings.fix: Add to the help: 'Some exceptions have a dollar limit that counts earlier years' withdrawals for the same purpose (birth or adoption, first home, emergency, domestic abuse). Answer Yes if this year plus earlier withdrawals go over the limit.'

findings.who: A filer whose payer coded 2 on a fact the payer cannot verify or got wrong. Examples: a separation from service in a year before the filer turned 55, or an IRA that was rolled over from a plan (the age-55 rule does not apply to IRAs). Another: a 457 distribution that comes from a rollover out of a qualified plan, or medical expenses below 7.5% of AGI.
findings.why_no: The help frames code 2 as the payer's knowledge of an exception. The filer defers to the payer's code instead of checking the exception's conditions, and answers no.
findings.irs_text: i5329 (2025) p. 5, exception 01: "Qualified retirement plan distributions (doesn't apply to IRAs) you received after separation from service when the separation from service occurs in or after the year you reach age 55". Exception 13: "Distributions from a section 457 plan, which aren't from a rollover from a qualified retirement plan."
findings.fix: Reword: 'Code 2 means the payer believes an exception applies, but the payer may not know all the facts. Does any part of this money fall outside the exception's conditions (for example age at separation, IRA versus employer plan, rolled-over money, or a dollar limit)?'

findings.who: Any code 2 filer reading the question as worded.
findings.why_no: 'Does that exception fail to cover all of this money (it covers only part of it, or none)?' is a negated question. A filer whose exception covers only part may answer no, meaning 'it does not cover all'.
findings.irs_text: i5329 (2025) p. 5, Line 2: "Enter on line 2 the amount that you can exclude."
findings.fix: Ask positively: 'Does the exception cover every dollar of this distribution?', with No ending the interview.

locators: p. 5, Line 2, "Enter on line 2 the amount that you can exclude."

findings.who: A filer whose Form 1099-R box 7 shows code 7 together with a second code, such as 7D, 7K, 7L, 7M, 7A or B7. The filer was under 59½ when the money was paid.
findings.why_no: No question is asked here. The gate tests the helper for equality with the single value 'normal_7'. If a combined code maps to another helper value, the gate is false. The age question is never asked, and the line is silently false.
findings.irs_text: i5329 (2025) p. 5, Line 2: "Enter on line 2 the amount that you can exclude." The exclusions there assume the 10% tax applies to a distribution received before age 59½. A code 7 issued to someone under 59½ is a payer error that the filer must still account for.
findings.fix: Make the gate 'box 7 contains code 7', alone or combined with another code, instead of equality with 'normal_7'. Or ask the age question for every Form 1099-R regardless of code.

findings.who: Joint filers where the Form 1099-R with code 7 belongs to the spouse, who was under 59½ when paid. The primary filer, who is entering the data, is over 59½.
findings.why_no: "Were you under age 59½ when you received any of this money?" The filer answers from their own age, not the recipient's.
findings.irs_text: i5329 (2025) p. 5, Line 2: "Enter on line 2 the amount that you can exclude." Each spouse who owes the additional tax files a separate Form 5329, based on the recipient's own age.
findings.fix: Ask: "Was the person who received this distribution (you or your spouse, as named on this Form 1099-R) under age 59½ on the date any of it was paid?"

findings.who: A filer who turned 59½ partway through 2025 (for example, born in late 1965) and received code 7 payments both before and after that date.
findings.why_no: The filer reads "under age 59½" as their age at year end, or reads "59½" as "59". They answer no, though earlier payments in the year came before 59½.
findings.irs_text: i5329 (2025) p. 5, Line 2, exception 12: "Include on line 2 the amount you received when you were age 59 1/2 or older." Age is tested on each payment date.
findings.fix: Add help text: "You reach 59½ six months after your 59th birthday. Answer yes if any payment in this form was made before that date, even if you were older by year end."

findings.who: A filer aged 59½ or older whose Form 1099-R shows code 1, J or S in error.
findings.why_no: The gate is false for these codes, so age is never asked. The line is set to false, which downstream logic may read as a known age fact rather than 'not asked'.
findings.irs_text: i5329 (2025) p. 5, Line 2, exception 12: "Distributions incorrectly indicated as early distributions by code 1, J, or S in box 7 of Form 1099-R. Include on line 2 the amount you received when you were age 59 1/2 or older."
findings.fix: Ask the recipient's age at payment for codes 1, J and S as well, and feed it to the line 2 exception 12 amount. Do not reuse a false from the code-7-only line as an age answer.

locators: p. 5, Line 2, "Enter on line 2 the amount that you can exclude."

findings.who: A married couple filing jointly. The spouse received the Form 1099-R with code 4 after the spouse's first husband died, and the spouse has since made that inherited IRA their own, for example by contributing to it. The primary filer is entering the spouse's form.
findings.why_no: The question asks 'are you the surviving spouse and have you made the IRA your own'. The filer at the keyboard is not the surviving spouse of the decedent and did nothing to the IRA, so the filer truthfully answers no.
findings.irs_text: i5329 p. 5, Line 2: 'Distributions due to death (doesn't apply to modified endowment contracts).' Exception 04 applies only to a beneficiary, not to a spouse who has made the IRA their own.
findings.fix: Name the recipient of this Form 1099-R: 'Did the person this Form 1099-R is for (you or your spouse) get this money some other way, or is that person the surviving spouse who has made the IRA their own...?'

findings.who: A filer whose Form 1099-R box 7 shows a combined code with 4, such as 4D, 4G, 4H, 4B, 4K, 4L, 4M or 4P. Examples are a surviving spouse whose deferred annuity shows 4D, or one whose direct rollover shows 4G.
findings.why_no: The helper 'Distribution code in box 7' takes one value. A filer who sees '4G' or '4D' may pick G or D, so the computed 'Code 4 (death)' is false and the question is never asked.
findings.irs_text: i5329 p. 5, Line 2: 'Distributions due to death' (exception 04); i1040gi p. 27: 'Distribution code T is shown in box 7 of Form 1099-R' shows that box 7 codes drive the treatment.
findings.fix: Let the box 7 helper take both characters, or ask 'Does box 7 contain a 4, alone or with a letter?' and compute is_death from that.

findings.who: A surviving spouse who made the inherited IRA their own by rolling it into their own IRA, not by electing, contributing or skipping an RMD, and who still receives a code 4 form for the distribution.
findings.why_no: The parenthetical lists three ways of making the IRA your own: 'by choosing to, by putting money into it, or by not taking a required minimum distribution'. A spouse who rolled it over reads the list as complete and answers no.
findings.irs_text: i5329 p. 5, Line 2: exception 04 'Distributions due to death' applies only to a beneficiary.
findings.fix: Add 'or by rolling it over into your own IRA' and write 'for example' before the list.

locators: pp. 27-30, lines 4a-5b: Exceptions 2-4, Lump-Sum Distributions, Insurance Premiums for Retired Public Safety Officers, Simplified Method
p. 5, Line 2, "Enter on line 2 the amount that you can exclude."

findings.who: A filer who bought a nonqualified commercial annuity with after-tax money from an insurer. The Form 1099-R has box 7 code D and an amount in box 5 or 9b, and no employer or IRA is involved.
findings.why_no: The gate is computed as kind ≠ 'plan', so any answer other than 'plan' counts as an IRA. A filer who has no employer plan picks whatever option is not 'employer plan' or 'pension', and the tool treats a private annuity as an IRA. The pension branch is never asked.
findings.irs_text: i1040gi p. 28, Lines 5a and 5b: 'Your payments are fully taxable if (a) you didn't contribute to the cost ... of your pension or annuity'; p. 30: 'Your cost is generally your net investment in the plan ... may be shown in box 9b of Form 1099-R.'
findings.fix: Compute the IRA gate from a positive IRA answer, not from '≠ plan'. Tie it to the checkable fact 'Is the IRA/SEP/SIMPLE box (next to box 7) on this Form 1099-R checked?' Route every other annuity, including a commercial annuity, to lines 5a/5b and the after-tax cost question.

findings.who: A self-employed person or employee whose employer set up a SEP or SIMPLE IRA. Their paperwork calls it a 'Simplified Employee Pension plan' or 'SIMPLE IRA plan'. They took a distribution, and part of it was an excess contribution paid back or went to an HSA (an HFD from a non-ongoing SEP).
findings.why_no: The account is funded by an employer and is called a 'pension plan', so the filer chooses 'pension, annuity or plan'. That turns the IRA gate false, and the IRA-only questions that end the interview are never asked.
findings.irs_text: i1040gi p. 26: 'an IRA includes a traditional IRA (which includes a traditional IRA that receives contributions from a simplified employee pension (SEP) arrangement) ... and a SIMPLE IRA'; p. 27, Exception 2(4)-(5): 'You had a 2024 or 2025 IRA contribution returned to you ... You made excess contributions to your IRA for an earlier year and had them returned to you in 2025.'
findings.fix: In the kind-of-account help, say that SEP IRAs, SIMPLE IRAs and Roth IRAs are IRAs even when an employer funds them. Also classify from the IRA/SEP/SIMPLE checkbox on Form 1099-R rather than from the filer's label.

findings.who: A filer aged 70½ or older with an individual retirement annuity bought from an insurance company. The trustee paid part of the distribution straight to a charity as a QCD.
findings.why_no: The product is sold and statemented as an 'annuity', so the filer chooses 'pension, annuity or plan'. The IRA gate is false, and the charity/HSA question that should end the interview is skipped.
findings.irs_text: i1040gi p. 27, Exception 3: 'If all or part of the distribution is a qualified charitable distribution (QCD), enter the total distribution on line 4a ... A QCD is a distribution made directly by the trustee of your IRA ... to an organization eligible to receive tax-deductible contributions.'
findings.fix: Add to the help: 'An individual retirement annuity is an IRA. If the IRA/SEP/SIMPLE box on the 1099-R is checked, choose IRA.'

findings.who: A retired public school teacher or government worker who takes distributions from a 403(b)(7) custodial account or a governmental 457(b). The custodian is an investment firm that also holds their IRA, and the plan has after-tax money or the retiree is a public safety officer paying health premiums.
findings.why_no: The account is held at a brokerage like an IRA, is 'individual', and has no employer on the statement, so the filer chooses IRA. The pension branch is never asked.
findings.irs_text: i1040gi p. 28: 'Pension and annuity payments include distributions from 401(k), 403(b), and governmental 457(b) plans'; 'An eligible retirement plan is a governmental plan that is a qualified trust or a section 403(a), 403(b), or 457(b) plan.'
findings.fix: State in the kind-of-account help that 401(k), 403(b) and 457(b) accounts are plans even when held at a brokerage. Better, classify by the Form 1099-R IRA/SEP/SIMPLE checkbox.

findings.who: A joint filer entering their spouse's Form 1099-R from a plan. The spouse retired on disability, or the spouse (not the filer) is a retired firefighter.
findings.why_no: 'Was any of this paid to you because you became disabled' and 'Are you a retired police officer, firefighter' use 'you', so a filer entering the spouse's form answers about themselves and says no.
findings.irs_text: i1040gi p. 28: 'If you are an eligible retired public safety officer ... you can elect to exclude from income distributions'; p. 27: 'If you (or your spouse if filing jointly) received more than one distribution...'
findings.fix: Word these as 'the person this Form 1099-R was issued to (you or your spouse)', or name the recipient from the form.

locators: p. 26, Lines 4a and 4b, IRA Distributions
pp. 27-30, lines 4a-5b: Exceptions 2-4, Lump-Sum Distributions, Insurance Premiums for Retired Public Safety Officers, Simplified Method

findings.who: A filer who made a nondeductible contribution to a traditional IRA for 2025 but took no distribution from a traditional IRA in 2025, for example because the only retirement distribution was from a 401(k) or pension.
findings.why_no: The gate looks only at the kind of account a distribution came from; with no traditional-IRA distribution the computed condition is false, so the basis question is never asked.
findings.irs_text: i8606 (2025) p. 2, Who Must File: 'You made nondeductible contributions to a traditional IRA for 2025.'
findings.fix: Broaden the gate to ask about traditional-IRA basis whenever the filer made nondeductible contributions, converted, recharacterized, or had a divorce or inheritance basis event, even without a traditional-IRA distribution.

findings.who: A filer who receives a distribution from a SEP or SIMPLE IRA and has basis in a traditional IRA, or has after-tax basis in the SEP or SIMPLE IRA itself.
findings.why_no: The account-kind helper is SEP or SIMPLE, not 'traditional_ira', so the gate is false; the question's 'traditional IRA' wording also invites reading SEP and SIMPLE IRAs out.
findings.irs_text: i1040gi (2025) p. 27, Exception 2: 'You received a distribution from an IRA (other than a Roth IRA) and you made nondeductible contributions to any of your traditional IRAs...'
findings.fix: Gate on any non-Roth IRA distribution when any traditional, SEP, or SIMPLE IRA has basis, and word the question to include SEP and SIMPLE IRAs.

findings.who: A joint filer whose spouse has basis in a traditional IRA, such as nondeductible contributions or an inherited IRA, and who receives a traditional-IRA distribution from that spouse's IRA.
findings.why_no: The gated question asks 'any traditional IRA of yours' and the help never mentions the spouse; the filer answers no for themselves, and the joint return drops the spouse's basis.
findings.irs_text: i8606 (2025) p. 2, Who Must File: 'You or your spouse transferred all or part of their traditional IRA...'
findings.fix: Ask 'you or your spouse' and include the spouse's traditional, SEP, and SIMPLE IRAs in the basis test.

findings.who: A filer who transferred or received all or part of a traditional IRA in 2025 under a divorce or separation agreement and the transfer changed the IRA basis, but who had no traditional-IRA distribution.
findings.why_no: A divorce transfer is not a distribution from a traditional IRA, so the gate computed from the distribution source is false and the basis question is skipped.
findings.irs_text: i8606 (2025) p. 2, Who Must File: 'You or your spouse transferred all or part of their traditional IRA in 2025 to the other spouse under a divorce or separation agreement where the transfer resulted in a change in the basis...'
findings.fix: Add a direct divorce-transfer basis trigger and do not require a distribution from a traditional IRA.

findings.who: A beneficiary who receives a distribution from an inherited traditional IRA that has basis, where the account-kind helper records the account as an inherited IRA rather than exactly 'traditional_ira'.
findings.why_no: The gate requires the account kind to equal 'traditional_ira'; an inherited-IRA category makes it false, so the basis question is not asked even though the help mentions inherited basis.
findings.irs_text: i8606 (2025) p. 2, Who Must File: 'You received a distribution from an inherited traditional IRA that has a basis.'
findings.fix: Treat inherited traditional IRAs as within the gate and do not require the account-kind value to be exactly 'traditional_ira'.

findings.who: A filer who rolled after-tax money from a qualified work plan into a traditional IRA in 2025 and took no distribution from a traditional IRA.
findings.why_no: The gate looks at the account the distribution came from; the work-plan rollover is not a traditional-IRA distribution, so the gate is false. The help's 'Form 8606 on any earlier return means Yes' also suggests no to a filer with no prior Form 8606.
findings.irs_text: i8606 (2025) p. 9, Line 2: 'You rolled over any nontaxable portion of your qualified retirement plan to a traditional IRA... Include the nontaxable portion on line 2.'
findings.fix: Ask directly about after-tax rollovers into traditional IRAs and do not require a traditional-IRA distribution or a prior Form 8606.

locators: pp. 27-30, lines 4a-5b: Exceptions 2-4, Lump-Sum Distributions, Insurance Premiums for Retired Public Safety Officers, Simplified Method

p. 2, Who Must File, "You received distributions from a traditional IRA in 2025 and your basis in these IRAs is more than zero", "You or your spouse transferred all or part of their traditional IRA in 2025 to the other spouse under a divorce or separation agreement where the transfer resulted in a change in the basis", and "You received a distribution from an inherited traditional IRA that has a basis"; p. 9, Line 2, "You rolled over any nontaxable portion of your qualified retirement plan to a traditional IRA"

findings.who: A surviving spouse receives a joint-and-survivor annuity after a retiree's death, or a beneficiary is paid by a plan after an employee's death, but the payer reports box 7 code 7 (normal) or another non-death code instead of 4. Some payers do this for continuing survivor annuities. The plan pays the annuity to two or more beneficiaries, or the employee died before August 21, 1996.
findings.why_no: The gate is computed from the box 7 code. The filer truthfully enters the code printed on the form, so the gate is false even though the facts are those of a death payment to a beneficiary.
findings.irs_text: i1040gi p.30: 'If you are the beneficiary of an employee who died, see Pub. 575. If there is more than one beneficiary, see Pub. 575 or Pub. 721 to figure each beneficiary's taxable amount.' i1040gi p.29: 'If you are the beneficiary of a deceased employee or former employee who died before August 21, 1996, include any death benefit exclusion...'
findings.fix: Ask a fact-based question for every pension or annuity (line 5) Form 1099-R, whatever the code: 'Are you receiving these payments because the person who earned the pension or annuity (an employee, former employee or retiree) died?' Set the gate when the answer is yes or the code includes 4.

findings.who: A beneficiary whose Form 1099-R shows a combined death code, such as 4D (death payment from a nonqualified annuity), 4G (direct rollover of a death payment) or 4H, or whose death payment is reported without a box 7 code.
findings.why_no: If the helper 'Code 4 (death)' matches only a bare '4', a combined code makes the computed gate false. A General Rule annuity with several beneficiaries, or one with a pre-1996 death benefit exclusion, then passes without the refusal.
findings.irs_text: i1040gi p.28: 'If your Form 1099-R doesn't show the taxable amount, you must use the General Rule explained in Pub. 939'; p.30: 'If there is more than one beneficiary, see Pub. 575 or Pub. 721 to figure each beneficiary's taxable amount.'
findings.fix: Define 'Code 4 (death)' as true when any box 7 code on the form is 4, including combinations with D, G, H, B or K. Also cover forms with no code through the fact-based question above.

findings.who: A survivor of a railroad employee or of a federal civil service retiree who receives a survivor annuity reported on Form RRB-1099-R or OPM's CSA/CSF 1099-R. The payment may have no box 7 death code, or the payment may be entered through a route the code-based helper does not read. The annuity is shared among several survivors, or the employee died before August 21, 1996.
findings.why_no: The gate exists only for a 'payment from a plan' with code 4. A filer whose form uses a different format, or carries no code 4, never reaches the gated questions.
findings.irs_text: i1040gi p.28: 'If you received a Form RRB-1099-R, see Pub. 575 to find out how to report your benefits.' p.30: 'If there is more than one beneficiary, see Pub. 575 or Pub. 721 to figure each beneficiary's taxable amount.'
findings.fix: Apply the same 'paid because the earner died?' question to RRB-1099-R and CSA/CSF 1099-R survivor annuities. If those forms are out of scope, refuse them.

findings.who: A filer, or the filer's spouse on a joint return, who has an IRA distribution and also a separate code 4 survivor pension from an employer plan.
findings.why_no: If the helper 'IRA distribution (lines 4a and 4b)' is evaluated for the whole return rather than for each Form 1099-R, any IRA distribution makes the gate false for the employer-plan pension as well.
findings.irs_text: i1040gi p.29: 'More than one pension or annuity. If you had more than one partially taxable pension or annuity, figure the taxable part of each separately.'
findings.fix: Evaluate both helpers on the same Form 1099-R entry (the IRA/SEP/SIMPLE box and the code 4 on that form), never across the return.

findings.who: A surviving spouse who receives a survivor annuity under a retiree's joint-and-survivor election.
findings.why_no: The gated question asks whether payments are 'guaranteed for a set period ... not a survivor's pension paid for your own life'. A survivor may not know whether the plan's form of payment includes a period-certain guarantee, and may answer no.
findings.irs_text: i1040gi p.30: 'On your annuity starting date, either you were under age 75 or the number of years of guaranteed payments was fewer than 5. See Pub. 575 for the definition of guaranteed payments.'
findings.fix: Add help text: 'Check your plan's payment election or the survivor notice. A Yes means the plan pays for a fixed number of years (for example, 10-year certain) whether or not anyone is alive.'

locators: pp. 27-30, lines 4a-5b: Exceptions 2-4, Lump-Sum Distributions, Insurance Premiums for Retired Public Safety Officers, Simplified Method

findings.who: A filer converted a traditional IRA to a Roth IRA at the same custodian, which re-registered the account. The Form 1099-R shows code 2 or 7, not G.
findings.why_no: They think of it as a conversion, not as money that 'went into another retirement account' or that they 'put into a retirement account'. In their view nothing moved.
findings.irs_text: i1040gi p.27, Exception 2: '3. You converted part or all of a traditional IRA or traditional SIMPLE IRA to a Roth IRA in 2025.' (see Form 8606); p.30: 'a rollover to a Roth IRA or a designated Roth account is generally not a tax-free distribution.'
findings.fix: Ask the Roth question regardless of the gate, or broaden the gate: 'Did you convert, roll over, or move any of this money into any retirement account, including a Roth IRA or a Roth account in the same plan or at the same firm?'

findings.who: A participant directly rolled a designated Roth 401(k) account to a Roth IRA. The Form 1099-R shows code H (direct rollover of a designated Roth account), not G.
findings.why_no: The gate is computed true only for code G. The fallback asks whether the filer 'put' the money into an account, and the plan sent it directly, so they answer that they put nothing in.
findings.irs_text: i1040gi p.30, Rollovers: 'Use lines 5a and 5b to report a rollover, including a direct rollover ... See Pub. 575 for more details on rollovers, including special rules that apply to rollovers from designated Roth accounts.'
findings.fix: Treat code H, and any direct-rollover code, like code G. Reword the fallback: 'Did you, or the plan or IRA on your behalf, move any of this money into a retirement account?'

findings.who: A filer took money out of a Roth IRA or a traditional IRA and redeposited it into the same IRA within 60 days.
findings.why_no: The gate says the money 'went into another retirement account'. They put it back into the same account, so they read 'another' as excluding their case.
findings.irs_text: i1040gi p.27, Exception 1: 'you rolled over part or all of the distribution from one: Roth IRA to another Roth IRA, or IRA ... to a qualified plan or another IRA ... Generally, a rollover must be made within 60 days.'
findings.fix: Say 'any retirement account, including the same account you took it from'.

findings.who: On a joint return, the spouse received the Form 1099-R and rolled part of it into an IRA, a Roth IRA, or a new account, partly in shares. The primary filer answers the interview.
findings.why_no: If the fallback asks 'did you put some of this money', the answering spouse truthfully did not.
findings.irs_text: i1040gi p.27: 'If you (or your spouse if filing jointly) received more than one distribution, figure the taxable amount of each distribution.'
findings.fix: Name the recipient on the form: 'Did [recipient name] put any of this money into a retirement account?' or 'you or your spouse'.

findings.who: A participant received employer stock or other property from a plan in kind. They rolled some of the shares into an IRA and kept or sold the rest.
findings.why_no: The question asks about putting 'money' into a retirement account. They moved shares, not money, so they answer no.
findings.irs_text: i1040gi p.30: 'a rollover is a tax-free distribution of cash or other assets from one retirement plan that is contributed to another plan within 60 days ... See Pub. 575 ... partial rollovers of property.'
findings.fix: Ask 'Did you put any of this distribution (cash, shares, or other property, or money from selling them) into a retirement account?'

findings.who: A filer received a distribution in late December 2025 and files in January or February 2026. Their 60-day window is still open, and they roll over the money in 2026, after answering, or intend to before the deadline.
findings.why_no: The past tense ('put', 'went') is truthfully no at interview time, or is read as limited to 2025.
findings.irs_text: i1040gi p.27, Exception 1: 'Generally, a rollover must be made within 60 days after the day you received the distribution ... If you rolled over the distribution into a qualified plan or you made the rollover in 2026, include a statement explaining what you did.'
findings.fix: Ask 'Did you put, or will you put within 60 days of receiving it (including in 2026), any of this money into a retirement account?'

findings.who: The IRS levied the filer's IRA or plan account and later returned the amount. The filer re-contributes it to an IRA in 2026, before the return's due date, or has not yet done so when filing.
findings.why_no: The re-contribution has not happened yet, or the filer does not see paying levied money back in as 'putting this money into a retirement account'.
findings.irs_text: i1040gi p.30, Rollovers: 'Generally, a rollover is a tax-free distribution of cash or other assets ... contributed to another plan within 60 days' (the levy-return contribution is a separate rule outside the quoted pages).
findings.fix: Ask the levy question regardless of the gate, or include 'paid back money the IRS returned after a levy' in the gate's help.

findings.who: A former spouse under 59½ received a QDRO distribution from a plan and kept the cash.
findings.why_no: They truthfully answer that none of it went into a retirement account. The QDRO question is never reached, so the tool cannot flag the QDRO facts that affect early-distribution tax treatment.
findings.irs_text: i1040gi p.30: 'You may owe an additional tax if you received an early distribution from a qualified retirement plan and the total amount wasn't rolled over. For details, see the instructions for Schedule 2, line 8 ... See Pub. 575 ... distributions under qualified domestic relations orders.'
findings.fix: Ask the QDRO question for every plan distribution, not only rolled-over ones, or confirm that QDRO handling outside rollovers is covered elsewhere.

locators: pp. 27-30, lines 4a-5b: Exceptions 2-4, Lump-Sum Distributions, Insurance Premiums for Retired Public Safety Officers, Simplified Method

findings.who: A filer who took a 401(k) or IRA distribution, spent the check or had 20% withheld from it, and within 60 days deposited an equal amount from savings into a traditional IRA.
findings.why_no: The gate asks whether 'this money' went into a retirement account, and the help says 'If all of it stayed with you, answer No.' The filer kept the distributed dollars and deposited different dollars, so a literal no is truthful.
findings.irs_text: i1040gi p. 30, Rollovers: 'From that result, subtract the amount of the rollover.' p575 p. 24: 'subtract the amount that was rolled over either directly or within 60 days of receiving the distribution.'
findings.fix: Ask: 'Did you or your spouse put any amount into a retirement plan or IRA within 60 days (or later under a waiver) as a rollover of this distribution, even with other money, such as savings that replaced tax withheld?' Change the help to: 'Using different money still counts. Answer No only if nothing was deposited.'

findings.who: A filer who left a job with a 401(k) loan outstanding. The plan offset the loan against the account (a qualified plan loan offset reported on Form 1099-R), and the filer deposited that amount into an IRA before the return's due date.
findings.why_no: No money was paid to the filer, so 'this money' and 'even if it was paid to you first' do not seem to apply. The filer may also read the 60-day frame elsewhere in the tool as excluding a deposit made months later.
findings.irs_text: p575 p. 23, Plan loan offset: 'if you have a qualified plan loan offset, you will have until the due date (including extensions) for your tax return for the tax year in which the offset occurs to complete your rollover.'
findings.fix: Add to the gate: 'including a loan from the plan that was offset against your account when you left the job or the plan ended.' Also extend the gated question's deadline to the return's due date for a qualified plan loan offset.

findings.who: A filer whose plan distributed stock or other property. The filer sold it and put the sale proceeds into a traditional IRA within 60 days.
findings.why_no: The filer received shares, not 'money', and deposited proceeds rather than the item distributed, so the filer may read 'this money' as not covering it.
findings.irs_text: p575 p. 23, Rollovers of property: 'you must either roll over the actual property distributed or sell it and roll over the proceeds... If you sell the distributed property and roll over all the proceeds, no gain or loss is recognized on the sale.'
findings.fix: Change 'this money' to 'this distribution (cash, stock, or other property), or the proceeds from selling it'.

findings.who: A filer who took a qualified birth or adoption distribution, or a first-home IRA withdrawal for a purchase that fell through, and later put the amount back into an IRA or plan.
findings.why_no: The filer thinks of this as repaying or returning a withdrawal, not as a 'rollover or a conversion'. The deposit may also come months later, in a different frame from the distribution.
findings.irs_text: p590b p. 28: 'Any contribution made to the eligible retirement plan as a repayment of a qualified birth or adoption distribution may be eligible for tax-free rollover treatment.' Also: 'This contribution is treated as a rollover contribution to the IRA.'
findings.fix: Add to the help: 'Repaying a birth or adoption withdrawal, or putting back a first-home withdrawal after the purchase was canceled or delayed, counts.'

findings.who: A filer whose plan moved the balance directly, trustee to trustee, to a new employer's plan or to an IRA (code G), or a nonspouse beneficiary whose inherited plan balance was transferred directly to an inherited IRA.
findings.why_no: The money never left the retirement system, so 'go into a retirement account again' reads as describing money that came out and went back in. The filer may think a mere transfer is not a rollover.
findings.irs_text: i1040gi p. 30, Rollovers: 'Use lines 5a and 5b to report a rollover, including a direct rollover, from one qualified employer's plan to another or to an IRA.' p575 p. 24: 'The transfer will be treated as an eligible rollover distribution.'
findings.fix: Add to the help: 'A direct transfer from the plan to another plan or IRA counts, including a transfer to an inherited IRA.'

findings.who: A filer who received a distribution in late 2025 and made the rollover deposit in January or February 2026.
findings.why_no: The filer may read the question as asking about 2025 events and answer no because the deposit happened in 2026.
findings.irs_text: i1040gi p. 27, Exception 1: 'If you rolled over the distribution into a qualified plan or you made the rollover in 2026, include a statement explaining what you did.'
findings.fix: Add to the help: 'Count a deposit made in 2026 for a 2025 distribution.'

findings.who: A couple filing jointly. The spouse is 52 and received a code 7 Form 1099-R, either from a former employer's 401(k) that the payer miscoded or from a governmental 457(b) plan. The filer entering the return is 62.
findings.why_no: The helper asks 'Were you under age 59½ when you received any of this money?' On a joint return the person typing reads 'you' as themselves. They were over 59½, so they answer no. The tool then skips the section 457 question and its refusal. A miscoded early distribution from a non-457 plan passes as a normal distribution, and the additional tax is never flagged.
findings.irs_text: i5329 (2025) p. 5, Line 2: 'Distributions from a section 457 plan, which aren't from a rollover from a qualified retirement plan.' (exception 12). The refusal in the gated help ('this tool does not figure the extra tax that may then be due') is the outcome that a wrong no suppresses.
findings.fix: Ask about the recipient on this Form 1099-R by name: 'Was [recipient named on this form] under age 59½ on the date any of this money was paid?' Or take the age from the recipient's date of birth already entered and compare it with the distribution dates. Do not rely on 'you'.

findings.who: A filer born in March 1966 who turned 59½ in September 2025. They received code 7 payments in May and in November 2025 and are completing the return in 2026.
findings.why_no: They read 'were you under age 59½' as their age now or at year end, or they look only at the later or larger payment. They answer no even though the May payment was received before 59½.
findings.irs_text: i5329 (2025) p. 5, Line 2, exception 12: 'Distributions from a section 457 plan, which aren't from a rollover from a qualified retirement plan.' Contrast exception 11: 'Include on line 2 the amount you received when you were age 59 1/2 or older.' Age is judged at each receipt.
findings.fix: Compute the answer from date of birth: anyone who reaches 59½ during 2025 or later gets the question. Or reword it: 'Was any payment on this form made before the date you turned 59½ (6 months after your 59th birthday)? Answer yes even if you are 59½ or older now.'

findings.who: A 59-year-old filer, still short of 59½, who received a code 7 distribution from a 401(k) or a 457 plan.
findings.why_no: They read '59½' loosely as 'in my late fifties' or 'age 59' and decide the early-distribution worry doesn't apply to them. A payer's code 7 ('normal distribution') reinforces that no is the safe answer.
findings.irs_text: i5329 (2025) p. 5, Line 2: 'The additional tax on early distributions doesn't apply to the distributions described next. Enter on line 2 the amount that you can exclude.' (exception 12, section 457 non-rollover)
findings.fix: Show the threshold date in the help: 'You reach 59½ six months after your 59th birthday. If you were born after [date], you were under 59½ for at least part of 2025.'

findings.who: A filer under 59½ who received a distribution from a governmental 457(b) plan, all of it from non-rollover deferrals, where the payer entered code 1 or code 2 in box 7 instead of code 7.
findings.why_no: The computed gate is false whenever box 7 is not code 7. The gate keys on the document's code rather than on the fact of a 457 non-rollover distribution, so the exception 12 question is never reached on this path.
findings.irs_text: i5329 (2025) p. 5, Line 2, exception 12: 'Distributions from a section 457 plan, which aren't from a rollover from a qualified retirement plan.'
findings.fix: Confirm that the code 1 and code 2 paths offer exception 12. If they do not, ask the section 457 question for any distribution received before 59½, whatever the box 7 code.

locators: p. 5, Line 2, "Enter on line 2 the amount that you can exclude."
